pages.text: <name> had been looking forward to the family trip for weeks. The sun was bright, the station buzzed with excitement, and luggage trolleys rolled past like mini adventures on wheels. Everything was going perfectly — until he wandered off for a snack and accidentally boarded the wrong train.

At first, he was thrilled. The train’s shiny blue carriages gleamed in the morning sun. But a few minutes in, <name> realized the seats didn’t match the family’s reservations, and the station signs whizzed past too quickly. “Oh no! This isn’t our train!” he whispered, heart thumping.

From the window, he spotted his younger sister, Meera, waving frantically on the platform. She had seen him climb aboard the wrong carriage and shouted, “<name>! Wait!” Panic mixed with excitement as <name> leapt to action. He had to get back — and fast.

The train slowed briefly at the next platform. <name> jumped down carefully, landing with a stumble but unharmed. Around him, people bustled, trolleys clattered, and a stray hat blew past. He spotted a station map near the ticket booth and realized the platform number for the correct train. His eyes narrowed in determination.

“Come on, Meera!” he called, and she sprinted over, backpack bouncing. Together, they dashed across the long platform, weaving between luggage carts and laughing passengers. A group of pigeons scattered as they ran, cooing loudly and nearly tripping Meera over their fluttering wings.

The station was massive, full of twists and turns. Signs pointed in all directions, but a small clue from a hanging clock helped <name> calculate the fastest route: the overhead bridge connecting to the right platform. They raced up the stairs, counting steps aloud to stay focused. Midway, Meera almost tripped, but <name> grabbed her hand just in time.

From the top, they could see the gold-and-blue family train ready to depart. Their eyes widened — it was leaving soon. “Almost there!” <name> shouted, and they dashed down the ramp. A stray shopping cart rolled past, and <name> leaped over it, landing safely on the platform.

They sprinted past ticket-checking staff, who waved encouragingly. The last stretch was the trickiest. The train had begun to pick up speed, and <name> noticed a small gap between it and the platform. “Jump on three!” he whispered. Together, they counted: one… two… three! Both leapt, landing inside a carriage with a soft thud.

“Phew! You made it!” Dad exclaimed, hugging them tightly. Mom laughed, brushing Meera’s hair back. “That was quite the adventure!” <name> grinned sheepishly. Sparing a glance out the window, he saw the wrong train disappearing in the distance. The platform, bustling crowd, and even the pigeons faded behind them.

As the train rolled into the countryside, everyone shared snacks and stories. <name> realized that mistakes could lead to thrilling adventures if he stayed calm, thought fast, and worked as a team. He looked at Meera and smiled. “Next time, I’ll double-check the train number,” he said. She laughed and nodded. Even though the day had started with panic, it ended with joy, laughter, and a sense of accomplishment. <name> felt proud — not just for catching the right train, but for thinking on his feet and turning a small accident into a memorable adventure.
